subject.title: fix: derive heap pressure thresholds from V8 heap limit

question: Should OpenClaw apply 60% warning and 75% critical thresholds to every effective V8 heap limit, including ordinary Node heaps, and which candidate should carry that policy?
rationale: The V8 limit is the correct runtime signal, but the exact global margins alter availability diagnostics for all installations and require maintainer intent rather than code inference.

options.title: Preserve ordinary-heap behavior
options.body: Scale only clearly enlarged heaps while retaining the historical defaults for ordinary Node heaps.

options.title: Adopt global ratios
options.body: Apply 60% and 75% everywhere after approving the wider compatibility and availability impact.

options.title: Redesign pressure policy
options.body: Pause both candidates and choose margins from measured headroom or combined heap and RSS evidence.

recommendation.title: Preserve ordinary-heap behavior
recommendation.body: Scale only clearly enlarged heaps while retaining the historical defaults for ordinary Node heaps.

likelyOwner.reason: The original classifier and fixed-default policy appear to date to this contributor's merged implementation, making them the strongest history-based routing candidate.
